chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Sa'id ibn Abdullah al-A'raj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who recites the Qur'an then forgets it, then recites it again then forgets it, is there any difficulty/sin upon him regarding this? He said: No.
ai.seo_question: Does forgetting the Qur'an after memorizing it constitute a sin in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that forgetting the Qur'an after memorization, even repeatedly, does not incur religious difficulty (haraj) or sin, emphasizing the natural human tendency to forget. This ruling highlights the distinction between intentional neglect and natural cognitive lapse, reassuring believers that the burden of memorization is not a source of perpetual anxiety. The response underscores the Shia scholarly view that ease and mercy are central to religious obligations regarding the Qur'an.

en.ammaar-muslim: [3/1550] al-Kafi: Ali b. Ibrahim from his father from Safwan from Sa’id al-A’raj who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who memorizes the Qur’an, then he forgets it, then he memorizes it (again), then he forgets it, is there on him any sin because of this? He (i.e. the Imam) said: No
